title: High-Availability Failover Architectures: Patroni, Raft Quorum, and Split-Brain Defense
realWorldScenario: During a network partition between AWS Availability Zones, an automated failover script promoted the read-replica to primary. However, the original primary was still alive and accepting writes from half the Kubernetes pods, resulting in catastrophic split-brain data corruption.
questionStatement: Design a resilient High-Availability (HA) architecture for PostgreSQL using Patroni and a Distributed Consensus Store (DCS) such as etcd or Consul. Explain Raft consensus quorum, leader leases, fencing mechanisms (STONITH / Watchdog), and how synchronous replication with quorum commit prevents data divergence.
expectedConcepts: Split-brain diverging transaction logs and data corruption
Patroni leader lease TTL and automated promotion
Linux Watchdog / STONITH fencing killing zombie primary
hints: Why is merging two divergent PostgreSQL primaries impossible after split-brain?
What does a Linux watchdog do if Patroni fails to refresh its DCS lease?
How does Raft majority quorum prevent two nodes from both acquiring the leader lease?
